answers.answer: Shuffle all 4 Conflict III cards and place them at the bottom; shuffle the 9 Conflict II cards and deal 5 on top; shuffle the 3 Conflict I cards and deal 1 on top. This makes a 10-card deck, ordered I, II, III; return the unused 2 I and 4 II cards to the box without looking.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 2: ‘Result: a 10-card Conflict Deck — 1 Conflict I on top, 5 Conflict II below it, 4 Conflict III on the bottom.’

answers.answer: In four-player play, the human starts at 1 VP; in three-player play, at 0 VP. In either case the human starts with 2 Agents on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board, 3 troops in the garrison plus 9 in supply, and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 6: Score marker on 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents on Leader, third beside board; three troops garrison, remaining nine in supply; take 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes, you may Reveal while Agents remain, but after Revealing your turns are skipped for the rest of Player Turns. Reveal effects come only from the Reveal boxes of cards still in hand that you reveal, not cards already played on Agent turns. During Clean Up, all cards in front of you from Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Agent turns are optional; after Reveal your turns are skipped; Reveal Effects resolve only just-revealed cards; Clean Up moves all cards in front of you to discard.

answers.answer: Resources from a Plot Intrigue played before placing your Agent can pay the entry cost. Resources granted after placement by the destination or played Agent card cannot pay that same entry cost. One card can send only one Agent, using one matching Agent icon; a card with no Agent icons cannot be played on an Agent turn and can only be revealed.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: a legal Plot can be played before placement and its pre-entry resources can pay; placement/card gains after placement cannot pay. Agent Turn: choose only one Agent icon; no-icon cards only on Reveal.

answers.answer: At a Combat space, all 3 troops recruited this turn plus up to 2 from the garrison can deploy, so the maximum here is 5; having four garrisoned does not raise the 2-troop limit. At a non-Combat space no troops deploy. Recruited troops come from your supply and are placed in your garrison before deployment.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: deploy any/all recruited this turn plus up to two from garrison at a Combat space; troop icon recruits from supply into garrison.

answers.answer: The Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to any space connected to an observation post where you currently have a Spy; it does not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to bypass another player's Agent on the destination. Gather Intelligence recalls your Spy from a connected post to draw a card, chosen immediately after Agent placement and before receiving space or card effects. The same Spy cannot pay for both, but two different Spies may be recalled for the two different effects on a placement.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Spies: Spy Agent icon sends without recall; Infiltrate bypasses another player; Gather Intelligence timing is immediately after placement; cannot recall the same Spy to both (Research Station example permits two).

answers.answer: Strength is 11 (2 troops × 2 = 4, one sandworm = 3, four swords = 4). If your final unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict you cannot participate in the Combat Intrigue window, which is for players with at least one unit there.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop 2, sandworm 3, sword 1; if last unit removed strength 0. Combat: only players with at least one unit may play Combat Intrigue.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing does not bar you from acting again if another player plays a card; the window closes when all players involved pass consecutively. After rewards, troops in the Conflict return to their supply (not garrison), sandworms return to the bank, and Combat markers reset to 0.
answers.evidence: Combat: ‘You are not required to pass just because you passed earlier’; resolve after consecutive passes. Resolve Combat: troops return to supply, markers reset, sandworms to bank.

answers.answer: For a tie for first, each tied player gets the second reward; nobody wins or takes the Conflict card. In a four-player game, if exactly two tie for first, the other players compete for the third reward; in a three-player game no other rewards are given. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tie for first pays second to each, nobody wins/takes card; four-player exactly-two tie exception; three-or-fewer gives no other rewards. Resolve Combat: 0 strength receives no reward.

answers.answer: Having one or more sandworms doubles your rewards once; two worms do not quadruple them. Taking control of a location and battle icons on won Conflict cards cannot be doubled. If the reward offers 1 VP for paying 3 spice, you may pay that cost a second time to gain a second VP (6 spice for 2 VP).
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: ‘one or more’ double; control and battle icons excluded; optional reward cost may be paid a second time, example 3 spice per VP.

answers.answer: After winning a Conflict and taking its card into your supply, check for a matching battle icon among your face-up Conflict or Objective cards. If found, you must flip the matching pair face down and gain 1 VP. At Endgame, the wild battle icon can match any one of the three icons in your supply; flip the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: when you win and take the card, check face-up Conflict or Objective cards; must flip matching pair; Endgame wild icon matches any one of three.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; falling below 2 loses it and reaching 2 again regains it. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained below 4 and earned again on returning to 4. The first to 4 also gains the Alliance token and 1 VP; that VP follows the token. Tying the holder does not steal it: an opponent must rise higher, which transfers the token and its VP.
answers.evidence: Scoring—Faction Influence: 2 Influence VP reversal; 4 Influence track bonus retention/re-earning; first to 4 Alliance VP; tie does not steal.

answers.answer: During your Reveal turn, Persuasion can be spent before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool it from multiple sources for one card or split one source across cards; unused Persuasion is lost. Acquire from the five-card Imperium Row or either Reserve stack at the cost shown at the card's top right; after acquiring a Row card, its replacement is immediately available if affordable. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: Reveal turn purchases and timing; pool/split, no carryover, replacement may be acquired, card goes face up to discard.

answers.answer: When a Maker space is unoccupied at Makers, add 1 spice to its bonus spot; visiting a Maker space collects all bonus spice there. Hooks are required only when the summoning effect specifies them; Hooks are retained, not spent. While the Shield Wall remains, no sandworm can be summoned to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin. Sandworms are placed directly in your Conflict quadrant, never in a garrison; removing the Wall permits summoning to any Conflict.
answers.evidence: Phase 4 Makers and Sandworms: accumulate 1 spice; Agent gains all; Hooks not universal prerequisite or spent; Shield Wall protects three locations; worms directly to Conflict.

answers.answer: At Recall, if any player has 10+ VP or the Conflict Deck is empty, Endgame is triggered. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then most VP wins. Rulebook resource tiebreakers, in order, are spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: end at end of round on 10 VP or empty deck; Endgame Intrigue first; tiebreak order spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup puts 2 of the 20 standard contracts face up and the remaining 18 face down in the bank. Shuffle 4 extra Intrigue cards into the Intrigue Deck and 4 extra Imperium cards into the Imperium Deck. Shaddam is an optional Leader choice, not compulsory. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are the Rise of Ix compatibility set and stay in the box; they are not part of standard CHOAM setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes: 20 contracts, two face up and 18 face down; add four cards to each deck; Shaddam optional. Contrasting-back contracts are separate Rise of Ix set.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts into your supply and replace it with a face-up contract from the bank. Without CHOAM, or when all contracts are taken, it gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract completes on a Maker-space Agent visit when you gain the listed amount of spice that turn in total, including other sources. Immediate completes as soon as taken. Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Taking contracts and Completing contracts sections.

answers.answer: No. If you take a contract for a space where you already sent your Agent this turn, you wait until a future turn because you must hold it when sending that Agent. On completion, announce it, gain its shown rewards, flip it face down, and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Completing contracts: must hold contract at time of Agent placement; completion announces, rewards, flips face down and remains in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. It gets the Ornithopter Objective; the two humans randomly receive the other two eligible Objectives, and the human with the First Player marker on their Objective starts. First Player alternates only between humans. Turn order each round is First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival takes Agent turns and never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup and Agent turns: one shared Rival; Ornithopter Objective; human first-player determination and turn order; Rival never takes Reveal.

answers.answer: If the indicated destination is occupied, ignore it and reveal another Hagal card. A Place Spy card places a Spy at an empty post of its specified type if possible, but does not place an Agent; then immediately reveal another card and continue this Agent turn. Ignore ordinary board-space costs and effects; apply only the revealed House Hagal effects. If the Hagal deck is empty or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle it and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: occupied destination → reveal again; Place Spy continues turn; ignore normal costs/effects; empty or Reshuffle causes immediate reshuffle.

answers.answer: For standard three- or four-player setup, shuffle Objectives after omitting cards whose 1-3P/4/6P marking does not match the player count, then each player draws one at random. The player whose Objective shows the First Player marker takes it. Shaddam Corrino IV is not used unless playing with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 3 and 5: do not use Shaddam unless with CHOAM; omit mismatched Objective cards, deal one per player, marker determines First Player.

answers.answer: Solari, spice, water and sandworms are not limited; if the bank runs out, make any convenient substitution. Troops are different: if your personal supply is empty, you cannot recruit more until troops return there. Resource payments return Solari, spice and water to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 7: resources and sandworms ‘not meant to be limited’; substitute if needed; gains from and payments return to bank. Recruiting: no supply troops means no recruitment until return.

answers.answer: The five phases are Round Start → Player Turns → Combat → Makers → Recall. At Round Start reveal the top Conflict and place it face up next to the deck, resolve any defensive troop bonus, then each player draws five cards. If Endgame is not triggered at Recall, return Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise, and begin the next Round Start.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure lists five phases; Phase 1 conflict then defensive bonus then five-card hand; Phase 5 recall and pass marker if no winner.

answers.answer: Yes. Space effects, Agent-box effects and the Faction Influence advance may be carried out in any order. You must meet requirements and pay costs before resolving any space or played-card effects, so the Influence from that visit cannot satisfy its own entry requirement.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs and meet requirements immediately before effects; effects and Influence may be done in any order.

answers.answer: An optional arrow cost can normally be paid only once per turn, so you cannot pay it twice for repeated effects; doubled Conflict rewards are the exception. Most card and space effects are mandatory. Optional cases include ‘may,’ arrow costs you can decline, and the black-X trash icon; direct self-trash instructions are mandatory. Intrigue conditions and costs must be met to play it.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Arrows / paying costs and FAQ—Mandatory effects and costs.

answers.answer: A Spy placement icon lets you put a Spy from supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have no Spies in supply, you may first recall one of your Spies for no effect. If the placement effect specifies an Agent-icon type that must connect to the post, you must meet that condition or cannot place the Spy.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Spies & observation posts: unoccupied post, recall if no supply Spy, some effects specify required connected Agent icon.

answers.answer: Infiltrate is described for bypassing another player's Agent, not your own occupied space, so using it on your own space is unsupported by this summary. You still need to play a card and send an Agent on an Agent turn; recalling a Spy alone cannot send one. You cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement; you may use two for different effects, one Infiltrate and one Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Infiltrate is defined as ignoring another player's Agent; FAQ says recalling a Spy does not waive playing a card for Agent turn; same Spy not both, and FAQ permits two different effects but never two Gather Intelligence recalls.

answers.answer: When any player visits a controlled Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, the controller gains 1 Solari; at Imperial Basin the controller gains 1 spice. The visitor also receives the listed visit effects. A player who wins the corresponding Conflict places their Control marker, replacing any opponent's marker. On reveal of a Conflict at a location already controlled, its controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to the Conflict without an Agent visit.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control and Board Space Guide: control bonus on any visit, winner places/replaces marker; defensive troop on reveal from supply.

answers.answer: In a three-player tie for second, each tied player takes the third reward; the Conflict winner keeps their reward and card, and no further rewards are given. Players tied for third get nothing. If three players tie for first in a four-player game, each takes second reward, nobody wins/takes the card, and no other rewards are given.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Combat ties: tie second gets third reward; tie third nothing; four-player three-or-more tied first gives no other rewards.

answers.answer: With three different positive strengths in a normal three-player Conflict, first and second receive rewards; third receives none. If a two-player game's Rival is a participant, it is treated as a three-player game including the Rival: ordinary first and second are paid, ordinary third is not, and third reward is used only in a tie for second.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: with 2 or 3 players (including two humans plus Rival), first and second paid; third only on tie for second.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues during Combat; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down and separate from your deck; after resolving, put them face up in a discard pile by the Intrigue Deck. If the Intrigue deck runs out, shuffle its discard to form a new deck.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Intrigue cards and FAQ—Draw timing.

answers.answer: An ordinary discard is a card of your choice from your hand; it cannot be an Intrigue unless specified. The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon lets you trash one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. Secrets steals one Intrigue selected at random from each opponent who has four or more Intrigues.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Discarding and Intrigue cards; Board Space Guide—Secrets effect.

answers.answer: Trash effects may remove cards from hand, discard pile, or in play. Return ordinary trashed cards to the box; return Reserve cards to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or directed to trash itself. Trashing The Spice Must Flow does not remove its acquired VP; that VP is retained.
answers.evidence: Actions—Trashing and FAQ—Victory: The Spice Must Flow acquire VP retained if later trashed.

answers.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once at the moment you acquire that card. When you cannot draw because your deck is empty, reshuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue drawing. Persuasion cannot be saved; unused Persuasion is lost during that Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Acquire box; Acquiring Cards: reshuffle when deck empty and Persuasion never saved.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and cards revealed on your Reveal turn remain face up and in play until Clean Up at the end of the Reveal turn, unless trashed first. Fremen Bond works if there is at least one other Fremen card in play; two Bond cards can activate one another regardless of play order. They cease being in play at Clean Up.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—In play / Fremen Bond.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent just sent this turn; you may use that recalled Agent on another Agent turn in the same round. Retreat moves a troop from Conflict to garrison. ‘Retreat any number’ includes zero.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Recall Agent; Retreat; FAQ—Combat and troops.

answers.answer: A single free-choice effect that grants two Influence requires choosing one Faction for both; you cannot split it. An Alliance icon requires you to hold that Faction's Alliance token. A minimum-Influence effect requires meeting the stated minimum on that Faction.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Influence: free-choice gain two cannot choose two Factions; Alliance and minimum Influence requirements.

answers.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied with two opponents, the former holder chooses which of the tied players receives the Alliance. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4 or more to take it, return the token to the board; the former holder loses its Alliance VP.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Alliance loss: if several were tied, former holder chooses; falling to 3 or lower loses Alliance; if nobody has 4+, return it; losing it loses VP.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used this turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, in addition to the five cards drawn then. A Plot Intrigue with a later Reveal effect stays face up until then, is used at Reveal, and is then discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Draw timing.

answers.answer: No. A ‘when you win a Conflict’ Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first because no one wins. If you receive such an Intrigue as a reward for an outright win, you may play it immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Combat and troops: winning-trigger Intrigues cannot be played after tie, but may be played immediately if received as reward for winning.

answers.answer: If VP and all four resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed 12-space track.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Victory: all-resource tie goes to most recent Reveal; scores may exceed printed track's 12.

answers.answer: No. Fulfill all contracts you hold for the same space with one Agent placement; you cannot delay some after visiting. The contract completion is another effect of that Agent turn and may resolve in any order with the space and Agent-box effects, but you must have held it when sending the Agent.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Contract completion is mandatory.

answers.answer: Shaddam does not begin with the set-aside Sardaukar contracts; Sardaukar Commander lets him choose a set-aside Sardaukar contract instead of a generally available one when acquiring a contract. His Emperor of the Known Universe deployment restriction takes effect immediately when playing Signet Ring to send an Agent and lasts only that turn, not the round.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Shaddam.

answers.answer: Feyd's token starts on the leftmost Training track space and stays on the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica begins with the Lady Jessica side face up. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Feyd-Rautha and Lady Jessica; FAQ says Reverend Mother Jessica may use ability on flip turn.

answers.answer: For Margot and Irulan, moving from 1 to 3 Influence counts as reaching 2; reaching 2 can happen again later after losing Influence and moving up again. Moving down through 2 does not count as reaching it. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild's Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications—Lady Margot / Princess Irulan and Spacing Guild's Favor.

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses the Spice Trade icon, has no cost, and draws a card; with CHOAM it also takes a contract, otherwise it gives 2 Solari (including when none remain). Dutiful Service uses the Emperor icon, has no cost, gives 1 Emperor Influence and takes a CHOAM contract or otherwise 2 Solari (including when none remain). Accept Contract gives no automatic Faction Influence; Dutiful Service explicitly gains Emperor Influence as an effect.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Accept Contract and Dutiful Service rows; guide preface says Accept Contract gives no automatic Influence.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City icon, no cost, Combat; visitor recruits 1 troop and draws a card, while controller gets 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen icon, no cost, Combat; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw a card. Research Station: City icon, costs 2 water, Combat; recruit 2 troops and draw 2 cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows: Arrakeen, Fremkit, Research Station.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two sandworms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one sandworm. Each also gives all accumulated bonus spice even when choosing worms. Hooks are retained and are not spent when summoning.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows for Deep Desert/Hagga Basin; Sandworms and FAQ: Hooks retained, not spent.

answers.answer: Sietch Tabr requires at least 2 Fremen Influence and is a City Combat space. Option one: if you lack Maker Hooks, take them; recruit 1 troop and gain 1 water. Option two: gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall. The second option does not grant a troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Sietch Tabr row.

answers.answer: High Council is a Landsraad, non-Combat space and costs 5 Solari each visit. On your first visit, place your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gain 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. On subsequent visits, gain 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit 3 troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—High Council row.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone gains a Swordmaster and 6 once anyone has one. Each player may visit only once per game. Take the third Agent from beside the board onto your Leader; it is available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival obtaining its Swordmaster also lowers the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Swordmaster row; Rival Rules says Rival's Swordmaster lowers human cost to 6.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses the Landsraad icon, requires 2+ Emperor Influence, and costs 3 Solari. Its effects: you may discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue; recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically give Emperor Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Imperial Privilege row; Special Rules says Influence is gained on actual Faction board spaces, and listed effects control.

answers.answer: Shipping uses the Spice Trade icon, requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence, and costs 3 spice. It gains 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction, which need not be the Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Shipping row.

answers.answer: Gather Support is Landsraad and non-Combat: choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari; recruit 2 troops either way, and if you pay 2 also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery is City Combat: choose no cost for 2 Solari or pay 1 spice for 4 Solari; its controller separately gains 1 Solari on a visit.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Gather Support and Spice Refinery rows.

answers.answer: Heighliner is Spacing Guild Combat, costs 5 spice, gains 1 Guild Influence and recruits 5 troops. Desert Tactics is Fremen Combat, costs 1 water, gains 1 Fremen Influence, recruits 1 troop and may trash a card. Sardaukar is Emperor but not Combat, costs 4 spice, gains 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue and recruits 4 troops; it does not allow normal deployment.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Heighliner, Desert Tactics and Sardaukar rows; Combat label marks deployment spaces.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall is Landsraad, no cost: draw an Intrigue and gain 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn if your Agent is there. Espionage is Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice: gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card and place a Spy. Deliver Supplies is Spacing Guild, no cost: gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water. None are Combat spaces.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Assembly Hall, Espionage and Deliver Supplies rows.

answers.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn; it can be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear's red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: False Orders and Litany Against Fear.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If it is not acquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings—Manipulate.

answers.answer: The two-player Rival starts with four Influence cubes at track bottoms, three troops in its garrison and the rest in supply, two Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside the board, three Spies and 1 water; its score and Combat markers are 0. Shuffle House Hagal retaining the 2P Reshuffle card. The Rival can trigger Endgame with 10+ VP at Recall and can win.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup and first paragraph.

answers.answer: As soon as the Rival's counted resources reach its printed Swordmaster value, it spends that many and takes its third Agent. Count Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water together at one each; spend Solari first, then spice, then Intrigue, then water, keeping leftovers. Its new Agent is usable in the current round.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Resources and Swordmaster.

answers.answer: After it has Swordmaster, the Rival spends a set of 7 Solari for 1 VP, or 7 spice for 1 VP, or 3 Intrigue cards for 1 VP, or 3 water for 1 VP. These are exact separate sets; a mixed total of seven resources is not specified as a scoring set.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Resources and Swordmaster: ‘whenever it has 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water, spend each such set for 1 VP.’

answers.answer: The Rival chooses the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by leftmost priority icon. It gains 1 VP at 2 Influence and Alliance VP transfers/retention work as for a human, but receives no resource track bonus for reaching 4. A numbered Hagal Influence icon means that numbered position in its Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival Rules—Resources, Combat and Hagal effects: influence VP/Alliances like human, no 4-influence resource bonus; choose least Influence; numbered icon refers to priority list.

answers.answer: No. For a two-destination Hagal card, use only the destination matching current conditions; if it is occupied, reveal a new card rather than using the other destination. The conditions are Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping and Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Agent turns.

answers.answer: Yes. At every Combat space the Rival deploys up to 2 available garrison troops even if the Hagal card recruited none; newly recruited troops also deploy there. At a non-Combat space, recruited troops go to garrison. A conditional 2+ Influence bonus that it cannot meet is simply omitted and does not prevent Agent placement.
answers.evidence: Rival Rules—Agent turns: troop icons; every Combat deploy up to two; conditional bonus absence never prevents placement.

answers.answer: Unless the post type is specified, the Rival uses the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy immediately recalls its other two and triggers its Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies to Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Rival Rules—Spies and Schemes.

answers.answer: If its Scheme recruits troops before Agent placement and the Rival then visits a Combat space that turn, deploy those Scheme-recruited troops too. If a Place Spy card finds no legal post, ignore placement, immediately reveal another Hagal card, and continue that Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Rival Rules—Spies and Schemes and Agent turns.

answers.answer: The Rival always collects all bonus spice at a visited Maker space. At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, with Hooks and an unprotected Conflict it summons one or two worms respectively instead of taking base spice; if it summons none, it takes base spice (Hagga 2, Deep Desert 4). Without Hooks, or when Shield Wall protection prevents summoning, it takes base spice. A Hagal Maker Hooks icon takes a token if needed.
answers.evidence: Rival Rules—Maker spaces.

answers.answer: At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal one Hagal card in turn order and add only its bottom swords to strength. If Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window, so may respond after the Rival's bonus is determined. With no deployed unit, the Rival gets no bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Rules—Combat.

answers.answer: Yes. Rival gains control bonuses, defensive troops, battle-icon VP and sandworm-doubled rewards normally. It takes optional Conflict VP whenever it can pay the resources or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; with CHOAM, a contract reward gives it 2 Solari.
answers.evidence: Rival Rules—Combat.

answers.answer: During Reveal Effects, total Combat strength, announce it, and set the Combat marker at any point while resolving; update it as needed, so it need not wait until the end. If strength exceeds 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure—Resolve Reveal Effects; Actions—Strength.

answers.answer: A Leader's Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns, not merely when you reveal it. Cards of any type can override the usual rules of the game.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 3: Signet Ring ability activates when played on Agent turn, not merely revealed. Overview: cards of any type can override usual rules.

answers.answer: The Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for a powerful effect. The icon itself does not automatically mean Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate no-card recall options with their own effects.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Spies: Recall Spy icon and separate Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence options.

answers.answer: The trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction instead discards a card of your choice from your hand and cannot select an Intrigue unless specified; ordinary discard does not trash it.
answers.evidence: Actions—Trashing; Special Rules—Discarding.

answers.answer: When a sandworm doubles a reward of one Influence of your choice, you may take that reward twice and choose the same or different Factions for the two separate one-Influence instances. This differs from a single effect granting two Influence, where a freely chosen Faction must be the same for both gains.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling example permits 2 Influence with same Faction or two different; Influence rule says one gain-two effect cannot split.

answers.answer: The Rival resolves its printed Signet Ring ability from the House Hagal effect. It does not require a human Signet Ring card or a Reveal turn; the Rival follows its Rival card's printed Signet Ring and Scheme abilities during Hagal Agent turns.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: follow Rival card's printed Signet Ring and Scheme abilities; it never Reveals. Inference: its Hagal Signet Ring effect is the applicable printed Rival ability.

answers.answer: A Hagal Maker Hooks icon takes a token if the Rival lacks one and has no effect if it already has Hooks. A Hagal Shield Wall removal effect removes the Wall only if the Rival has Maker Hooks; without Hooks it is ignored. If the Wall is already gone, there is no token to remove, so it has no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Rules—Maker spaces: Hooks icon takes token if needed; Shield Wall removal removes only if Rival has Hooks, otherwise ignore. The already-gone case is not explicitly stated; no additional effect is described.

answers.answer: Secrets uses the Bene Gesserit icon, costs nothing, and is not a Combat space. It gains 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draws an Intrigue from the deck; additionally, each opponent with 4+ Intrigues gives you one selected at random.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Secrets row.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses the Spice Trade icon, has no entry cost, and is a Combat space. Visitor gains 1 base spice plus all accumulated bonus spice; if that same player controls it, controller separately gains 1 spice, for total 2 base plus the bonus spice.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide preface says resolve visitor and controller bonuses even if same player; Imperial Basin row gives visitor 1 base and all bonus, controller 1 spice.

answers.answer: Reveal the new Conflict from the top of the deck and place it face up next to the deck on top of any Conflict cards left from previous rounds. The defensive troop bonus is resolved if applicable, then each player draws five cards; thus Conflict is revealed before the round's five-card hands are drawn.
answers.evidence: Phase 1: Round Start.

answers.answer: Place one human cube on the bottom space of each of the four Faction Influence tracks; place Alliance tokens on the marked areas of those four tracks. No human starts with an Alliance token. The Shield Wall token is initially placed on the marked area below Spice Refinery.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 1 and 6: Alliance tokens placed on tracks, cubes at bottom spaces, Shield Wall placed below Spice Refinery.

answers.answer: The First Player takes the first turn, then play continues clockwise. A player who Reveals is skipped for the rest of Player Turns; in standard 3–4 player play, the phase ends when all players have Revealed. During Combat Intrigue, First Player has priority, then clockwise; players with a unit in Conflict may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards or pass, and the window resolves after all involved players pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Player Turns and Combat sections of Turn Structure.

answers.answer: Reveal turn steps are: (1) Reveal Cards; (2) Resolve Reveal Effects; (3) Clean Up. Reveal-box effects may be resolved in any order; Persuasion may be used before, between or after them.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure—Reveal Turn lists three steps and says resolve effects in any order.

answers.answer: Each human shuffles the ten-card starting deck listed in Components and places it face down to the left of the Leader. Shuffle the Intrigue Deck and place it face down; shuffle the Imperium Deck and deal five face up for the Imperium Row; place Reserve cards in Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow stacks. Without CHOAM, omit CHOAM-marked cards. The human Combat marker starts at 0; three Spies and Councilor token are in supply; Control markers are in supply.
answers.evidence: Components—Starting deck; Setup, steps 4 and 6: prepare decks/Row/Reserve and place Combat marker at 0, remaining components including Spies in supply.

answers.answer: During a Reveal turn, ordinary Persuasion purchases may acquire any of the five Imperium Row cards or either Reserve card, Prepare the Way or The Spice Must Flow. Each cost is shown at the card's top right.
answers.evidence: Actions—Acquiring Cards.

answers.answer: Yes. Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional, so a player may decline even with a legal placement or recall. The Shield Wall detonation icon also says you may remove the token, so destruction is optional. Once removed it returns to the box; whether it can return in a later round is unsupported by the summary.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Spies says ordinary placement and recall optional; Shield Wall says may remove token and return it to box, but does not state whether it can return later.

answers.answer: Ordinarily the played card must have an Agent icon matching the destination's upper-left icon. A connected Spy by itself does not let a card with only a City icon send to Shipping. If the card has the Spy Agent icon, it can send to any space connected to an observation post where you currently have a Spy; the Spy is not recalled.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn and Spies: connected Spy does not grant every card Spy access; Spy Agent icon permits connected space.

answers.answer: Yes. On your Agent turn you may first play a legal Plot Intrigue; resources it grants before placement may pay the destination cost. Resources granted only after placement by the card played to send the Agent or by the destination cannot pay for that same entry cost.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot before placement resources may pay; Agent turn requires cost before resolving destination or played-card effects.

answers.answer: No. In two-player play, after both humans have Revealed, continue the Rival's Agent turns while it has Agents in supply; go to Combat only after both humans have Revealed and the Rival has used all its Agents. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Phase 2: Player Turns, two-player play.

answers.answer: Standard 2–4-player board spaces and Combat status: Accept Contract—Spice Trade, no; Arrakeen—City, yes; Assembly Hall—Landsraad, no; Deep Desert—Spice Trade, yes; Deliver Supplies—Spacing Guild, no; Desert Tactics—Fremen, yes; Dutiful Service—Emperor, no; Espionage—Bene Gesserit, no; Fremkit—Fremen, yes; Gather Support—Landsraad, no; Hagga Basin—Spice Trade, yes; Heighliner—Spacing Guild, yes; High Council—Landsraad, no; Imperial Basin—Spice Trade, yes; Imperial Privilege—Landsraad, no; Research Station—City, yes; Sardaukar—Emperor, no; Secrets—Bene Gesserit, no; Shipping—Spice Trade, no; Sietch Tabr—City, yes; Spice Refinery—City, yes; Swordmaster—Landsraad, no.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table lists all spaces and marks Combat spaces; guide preface identifies four Faction icons and non-Faction icons.

answers.answer: At Round Start, immediately when a Conflict is revealed for a location you already control, you may deploy one troop from your supply directly to the Conflict without visiting the location; taking the defensive bonus is optional. After all Combat rewards, return troops to supply, return sandworms to the bank, and reset all Combat markers to 0 before Makers.
answers.evidence: Phase 1 defensive troop bonus; Critical Locations & Control; Resolve Combat cleanup.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you and send one Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied matching board space. Resolve its Agent box, ignoring the Reveal box, along with the space effects. You cannot reuse a card already in play or take one from discard, and the Agent sent must come from your Leader; an Agent already on the board is not simply moved. Spies can separately allow access/bypass as described.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: card from hand, Agent from Leader, matching unoccupied space, use Agent box only; Clean Up moves played cards to discard.

answers.answer: No. Emperor of the Known Universe takes effect immediately when Shaddam plays Signet Ring to send the Agent; resolving board-space effects first cannot postpone the deployment restriction. Follow the printed Leader restriction.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications—Shaddam: restriction takes effect immediately on playing Signet Ring to send Agent; effect-order freedom cannot postpone it.

answers.answer: With four players and four different positive strengths, first, second and third place receive the corresponding printed rewards; fourth place receives no reward. The highest-strength player wins the Conflict and takes the Conflict card into their supply.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: four-player ordinary first, second and third receive rewards; highest strength wins and gains first reward and Conflict card.
